findings.description: Requirements schema validation is currently enforced via pytest in CI; adding local pre-commit hook validation provides immediate developer feedback.
findings.impact_analysis: Low severity. Schema correctness is 100% enforced in CI, but developer ergonomic feedback latency is elevated when malformed JSON is committed locally before pushing.
findings.remediation_scope: Configure pre-commit hook binding for fast-path JSON schema validation across docs/pipeline/ and docs/dossiers/.
reverification_criteria: Local pre-commit hook automatically rejects invalid JSON payloads with descriptive line/column errors.
Hook execution completed in <= 150ms on standard developer workstation.
Zero regressions on existing CI validation pipeline.
findings.root_cause: Schema linting was integrated into repository-level pytest test suites, but developer git hook configurations did not bind automated JSON schema validation to the local pre-commit hook stage.
findings.title: Automated JSON Schema Linting in Pre-Commit Hooks

findings.description: MISRA deviation permits are tracked in central JSON files; an automated tool scraping inline PRQA/Cppcheck comments into the dossier would streamline audits.
findings.impact_analysis: Low severity. 100% MISRA mandatory rule compliance is verified; automated scraping streamlines assessor walkthroughs.
findings.remediation_scope: Implement automated parser in static analysis toolchain to extract inline suppressions and format audit appendix.
reverification_criteria: 100% match between inline C comment suppressions and generated MISRA audit appendix.
Zero unmatched or unreferenced inline suppression tags.
findings.root_cause: MISRA compliance tracking relies on central reporting (_src/tools/misra_checker.py), but inline compiler suppression comments in C source units require manual cross-referencing during formal auditor interviews.
findings.title: Automated MISRA Inline Suppression Documentation Scraper

findings.description: QEMU virtual ECU platform currently models CAN controller and timer peripherals; adding SPI flash and crypto co-processor emulators will expand integration coverage.
findings.impact_analysis: Low severity. Current baseline functional requirements are fully verified; hardware register emulation is beneficial for next-generation silicon platform.
findings.remediation_scope: Accepted residual risk for Release v0.7.0; scheduled for implementation in Next Major Baseline v0.8.0.
reverification_criteria: Risk logged in Risk Register (RISK-0018-03) with residual severity LOW.
Reviewed and accepted by Project Lead and Lead Assessor.
Formal tracking in project roadmap for v0.8.0 development cycle.
findings.root_cause: Virtual ECU integration environment targets ARM Cortex-M7 with standard peripherals; dedicated cryptographic hardware accelerators (HSM) are emulated in software stubs rather than full hardware register emulation.
findings.title: Virtual QEMU Peripheral Hardware Emulation Model Expansion

findings.description: Earned Value metrics are tracked in JSON reports; printing an ASCII EV trend curve in CLI output improves visibility during daily standups.
findings.impact_analysis: Low severity. Management control and monitoring are 100% compliant; visualization improves team sync efficiency.
findings.remediation_scope: Add terminal ASCII trend sparkline rendering to project management CLI reports.
reverification_criteria: Deterministic sparkline rendering across Linux/macOS terminals without third-party graphics dependencies.
Verified by unit test in test_ecu_pilot_execution.py.
findings.root_cause: Management tracking engine (ecu_pilot_execution.py) calculates EV metrics deterministically, but output format was restricted to raw numbers and JSON logs without terminal sparkline visualization.
findings.title: Automated Sprint Earned Value Visualization in CLI Summary

findings.description: Measurement process tracks historical defect density; incorporating ARIMA predictive modeling will improve pre-release risk forecasting.
findings.impact_analysis: Low severity. Current statistical control charts fully satisfy ASPICE Level 2 measurement requirements.
findings.remediation_scope: Accepted residual observation for pilot baseline; scheduled for Level 3 multi-project organizational rollout.
reverification_criteria: Documented in measurement plan as Level 3 process maturity roadmap item.
Reviewed and signed off by QA Manager and Lead Assessor.
findings.root_cause: Process measurement uses standard statistical process control (+-3 sigma); advanced predictive time-series models were scoped for enterprise multi-ECU deployment rather than single pilot ECU.
findings.title: Automated Defect Density Forecasting using ARIMA Models
